prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1434; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your name for the recording.
A: I'd rather you not use my name on this one, if that's okay. Just call me the driver.
Q: That works for the file. Can you tell me where the accident happened?
A: It was on a two-lane road in Sugar Land, Texas, near a shopping center. Traffic was light.
Q: What were you doing right before the collision?
A: I was heading east, slowing down for a turn. The other car came over into my lane.
Q: How fast would you estimate you were going?
A: Maybe twenty-five miles an hour, maybe less. It wasn't a hard hit. Both cars were moving slowly.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, always.
Q: Did the airbags deploy?
A: No, they didn't. It felt more like a hard bump and a jolt forward and back.
Q: Did you get checked out by anyone after the accident?
A: I went to urgent care that afternoon. They looked at my neck and right shoulder and took some X-rays.
Q: Where exactly is the shoulder pain?
A: It's in the front and top of my right shoulder. It hurts when I reach overhead or lift anything heavy.
Q: Have you had any prior problems with that shoulder?
A: Nothing serious. I had some soreness from lifting a few years ago, but it went away with rest.
Q: Are you currently receiving treatment?
A: I'm going to physical therapy twice a week, and the doctor has me on anti-inflammatory medication.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm still working on getting back to normal. Some days are better than others.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
A: Thank you.
